 By Anjali Anand 
 Oct 27, 2026
 HFCL (NSE:HFCL) Lays Out Fibre, Preform and Defence Expansion Plans on Q2 FY27 Earnings Call
 Source: Shutterstock
 You are reading a free article with opinions that may differ from the recommendation given by Kalkine in its paid research reports. Become a Kalkine member today to get access to our research reports, in-depth technical and fundamental research. Learn More 
 Highlights 
 HFCL has filed the record of its Q2 FY27 earnings call held on October 19, 2026.
 Management said the order book stands at ₹28,900 crore.
 Cable capacity is being expanded from 39 million fibre kilometres to 63 million fibre kilometres in stages.
 The Government of Andhra Pradesh has allotted 1,000 acres for an ammunition manufacturing complex.
 What HFCL Has Filed
 HFCL Limited, listed on the NSE under the symbol HFCL and on the BSE under scrip code 500183, filed the record of its conference call on the unaudited results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, with the stock exchanges on October 26, 2026. The call was held on October 19, 2026. The filing was made under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and signed by Manoj Baid, President and Company Secretary.
 Mahendra Nahata, Promoter and Managing Director, addressed most questions. This article covers operational points and leaves out financial figures.
 Order Book
 Management said on the earnings call, “Our order book stands at ₹28,900 crore, providing multi-year revenue visibility.”
 Demand Drivers
 According to management, “Demand continues to accelerate across AI infrastructure, hyperscale data centres and telecom networks.” It also expects demand from telecom operators to increase and said the company is “talking to international telcos also where we think we’ll get some orders.”
 Fibre and Cable Capacity Expansion
 Management described a staged expansion of the company’s optical fibre and cable capacity. Fibre capacity is going from 28 million to 38 million and then to 43 million, though no unit was stated for these figures. Cable capacity is going from 39 million fibre kilometres to 56 million and then to 63 million fibre kilometres.
 Management said, “Fiber runs 100% of the capacity.”
 The company is also adding capacity for data centre connectivity solutions. Management said it is “introducing more products than only the fiber-based products,” covering other products required inside data centres.
 Preform and Backward Integration
 A preform is a high-purity glass rod from which optical fibre is drawn. Making it in-house reduces reliance on outside suppliers.
 Management referred to a “planned investment of approximately ₹1,800 crore across optical fiber, cable and preform manufacturing.” On the 600-tonne preform facility, it said there is “no headwind as such” and that the “October ’28 timeline which we have given, that would be met.”
 It added that the company’s own preform would cover “roughly about half of the capacity,” with the rest bought from outside under some long-term contracts. A mid-term solution for own preform is to start from the first quarter of next year. The company is also in talks with suppliers of germanium, which it expects to need in about two years.
 Defence and Aerospace
 Management described defence and aerospace as “HFCL’s next major engine of growth.” The portfolio spans thermal weapon sights, electronic fuzes, surveillance radars and multi-mode hand grenades.
 In September, the company delivered the second batch of thermal weapon sights for AK-203 to the Indian Defence Forces. Management said it has participated in a tender for 800,000 multi-mode hand grenades.
 On radars, one trial of the foliage penetration radar has taken place, with a second expected in about two weeks. The company has participated in a large tender for a drone detection radar in Chambal, and expects export orders for its ground surveillance radar. Both radars are indigenously designed.
 Management also said, “We expect to complete the acquisition during the current quarter,” referring to an aerospace acquisition.
 Ammunition Complex in Andhra Pradesh
 HFCL is setting up an ammunition manufacturing complex in Andhra Pradesh. Management said the “Government of AP has already allotted us 1000 acres of land parcel to set up this complex.” Construction is expected to start soon, and the hand grenades under the tender would be made at this site.
 Key Insights
 HFCL’s Q2 FY27 call points to expansion on two fronts. In optical fibre, the company is raising cable capacity to 63 million fibre kilometres and building a 600-tonne preform facility, with an October 2028 timeline, under a planned investment of about ₹1,800 crore. In defence, it delivered a second batch of thermal weapon sights, is pursuing radar programmes and is setting up a 1,000-acre ammunition complex in Andhra Pradesh. The order book stands at ₹28,900 crore.
 FAQs
 Q: What is HFCL’s order book? 
A: Management said the order book stands at ₹28,900 crore.
 Q: How is cable capacity being expanded? 
A: From 39 million fibre kilometres to 56 million and then to 63 million fibre kilometres.
 Q: When is the preform facility expected? 
A: Management said the October 2028 timeline for the 600-tonne preform facility would be met.
 Q: What is planned in Andhra Pradesh? 
A: An ammunition manufacturing complex on 1,000 acres allotted by the state government.
 Q: Which defence products does HFCL make? 
A: Thermal weapon sights, electronic fuzes, surveillance radars and multi-mode hand grenades.
